blocks.text: PCA and SVD both genuinely find structure entirely from the input features themselves, with no regard for any target variable at all, purely unsupervised techniques. LDA, Linear Discriminant Analysis, breaks from that pattern directly, using the actual target class labels to find projection directions that genuinely separate classes from each other as clearly as possible, rather than directions that simply capture the most overall variance.

This topic covers the genuine, different goal LDA pursues compared to PCA, the between-class and within-class variance ratio it actually maximizes, directly echoing the ANOVA F-statistic from the Feature Selection module, a real, structural limit on how many components LDA can ever produce, the assumptions this technique relies on, when to genuinely prefer it over PCA, and its genuine, dual role as both a projection technique and a classifier in its own right.
1. A Genuinely Different Goal Than PCA

blocks.alt: PCA maximizes variance while LDA maximizes class separation

blocks.text: PCA genuine goal is finding directions of maximum overall variance, entirely blind to which class any given row actually belongs to. LDA genuine goal is finding directions that best separate the different classes from each other, directly using those class labels as part of the actual computation, not as an afterthought.

This distinction genuinely matters in practice, a direction capturing enormous overall variance is not automatically a direction that separates classes well, and LDA specifically optimizes for the latter, genuinely more useful goal when the eventual downstream task is classification.
2. The Ratio LDA Actually Maximizes

blocks.alt: Between-class spread over within-class spread forms the ratio LDA maximizes

blocks.text: LDA genuinely maximizes a ratio, the variance between different class means divided by the variance within each individual class, directly echoing the exact F-statistic ratio covered back in ANOVA. A projection direction that spreads class means far apart, while keeping each individual class tightly clustered, genuinely produces a high value for this ratio, and is exactly what LDA searches for.

This connection to ANOVA is genuinely worth holding onto directly, LDA is not introducing some unrelated, new statistical idea, it is applying that same between-group versus within-group variance logic, now used to find an actual projection direction rather than just to score a single existing feature.

blocks.title: Worth remembering
blocks.content: LDA genuine optimization goal is mathematically the exact same idea as the ANOVA F-statistic covered in Feature Selection, between-group variance over within-group variance, just used here to find a projection direction rather than score one existing feature.

blocks.text: 3. A Real, Structural Limit on Components

blocks.alt: The number of classes minus 1 sets the maximum LDA components

blocks.text: LDA genuinely can produce at most k minus 1 components, where k is the number of genuine classes in the target, a binary classification problem, two classes, genuinely allows for only a single LDA component at most. This is a genuinely real, structural mathematical constraint, not a practical guideline that can be adjusted, unlike PCA, which can genuinely produce as many components as there are original features.

This real limit is worth knowing up front, LDA is genuinely not a general purpose dimensionality reduction tool the way PCA is, its usefulness genuinely depends on how many classes the actual target has.

blocks.text: 4. A Worked Example

blocks.alt: Two classes project through LDA into a clear separation

blocks.text: Applying scikit-learn LinearDiscriminantAnalysis for dimensionality reduction shows this genuinely supervised projection directly, on a small classification dataset.

code.content:
from sklearn.discriminant_analysis import LinearDiscriminantAnalysis
import pandas as pd

X = pd.DataFrame({
    "square_feet": [900, 1200, 1500, 1800, 2100, 2400],
    "bedrooms": [2, 3, 3, 4, 4, 5],
})
y = pd.Series([0, 0, 0, 1, 1, 1])

lda = LinearDiscriminantAnalysis(n_components=1)
projected = lda.fit_transform(X, y)

print(projected)

blocks.text: With only 2 genuine classes here, LDA genuinely produces just a single component, exactly the k minus 1 limit covered above, and that one component genuinely separates the two classes cleanly, unlike PCA, which would have optimized for overall variance without any regard for that real class separation at all.

blocks.title: A practical habit
blocks.content: Scale features before fitting LDA too, exactly the same discipline established for PCA and Lasso earlier in this course, since the underlying variance computation is genuinely sensitive to feature scale here as well.

blocks.text: 5. The Real Assumptions Behind LDA

blocks.alt: LDA assumes normally distributed classes with equal covariance

blocks.text: LDA genuinely works best when each class values are roughly normally distributed, and when every class genuinely shares a similar covariance structure, directly echoing the exact same assumptions covered back in ANOVA. When these assumptions are genuinely badly violated, a class with a wildly different spread than the others, for instance, LDA results can become genuinely less reliable.

This is worth taking seriously as a real, honest caveat, exactly like ANOVA before it, LDA output should not automatically be trusted as an absolute truth when its underlying assumptions clearly do not hold for a specific, real dataset.
6. When to Genuinely Prefer LDA Over PCA

blocks.alt: Having class labels available points to preferring LDA

blocks.text: LDA genuinely makes the most sense specifically when the downstream goal is classification, and preserving how well the classes separate from each other matters more than preserving genuine, overall variance in the data. PCA, by contrast, genuinely remains the more appropriate, general choice whenever there is no target label available at all, or when the downstream task genuinely does not care about class separation specifically.

This is a genuinely practical, real decision point worth internalizing directly, having target labels available does not automatically mean LDA is the better choice, it depends specifically on whether class separability is genuinely the property that actually matters for the real, downstream task.

blocks.text: 7. A Genuine Dual Purpose: Projection and Classifier

blocks.alt: LDA serves both as a dimensionality projection and as a classifier itself

blocks.text: Beyond dimensionality reduction, this topic entire focus, LDA can genuinely also be used directly as a classifier in its own right, predicting class labels for new data, not just projecting features into a lower dimensional space. This dual purpose genuinely exists because the same underlying, between versus within class variance computation that finds a good projection direction can also directly support classification decisions.

This classifier use case sits outside this topic direct scope, but is genuinely worth knowing about, LDA reappears later in this course specifically as a classification algorithm, built on the exact same underlying mathematics covered here.
8. LDA Versus What Comes Next

PCA, SVD, and LDA together cover the genuine linear projection techniques this module has built up so far, unsupervised variance maximization, its underlying general matrix operation, and supervised class separation. All three, though, genuinely share one real limitation, they can only find straight line, linear projection directions.

The next topic, t-SNE, introduces a genuinely different, nonlinear family of technique, one built specifically for visualization rather than general preprocessing, capable of capturing genuinely curved, complex structure that no linear projection covered so far in this module could ever represent.

items: LDA genuinely uses target class labels directly, unlike the purely unsupervised PCA and SVD.
It genuinely maximizes the ratio of between-class variance to within-class variance, echoing the ANOVA F-statistic.
LDA genuinely produces at most k minus 1 components, a real, structural limit tied to the number of classes.
It relies on the genuine same normality and equal covariance assumptions first covered back in ANOVA.
LDA genuinely makes the most sense when the downstream goal is classification and class separability matters most.
Beyond dimensionality reduction, LDA can genuinely also be used directly as a classifier in its own right.
